content.content:
User asks: "Who were the heads of state of the belligerents in the War of the Third Coalition and when did they die?" Need to list heads of state of each belligerent (countries involved) in War of the Third Coalition (1805). Belligerents: Third Coalition: United Kingdom, Austria, Russia, Sweden, Naples (Kingdom of Sicily/ Naples), Ottoman Empire? Actually Ottoman was not part. The main coalition: United Kingdom (King George III), Austria (Francis II), Russia (Tsar Alexander I), Sweden (King Gustav IV Adolf), Kingdom of Naples (Ferdinand IV). Also possibly the Kingdom of Portugal? Portugal was allied with Britain but not a main coalition member. Also maybe the Kingdom of Sicily (Ferdinand). Also the Republic of Venice was dissolved. Also the Ottoman Empire remained neutral. So we list heads of state: United Kingdom - King George III (reign 1760-1820, died 29 Jan 1820). Austria - Emperor Francis II (also Holy Roman Emperor Francis II; died 23 August 1835). Russia - Tsar Alexander I (died 1 December 1825). Sweden - King Gustav IV Adolf (died 7 February 1837). Kingdom of Naples (and Sicily) - Ferdinand IV of Naples (also Ferdinand III of Sicily, later Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies) died 4 January 1825. Also maybe the Kingdom of Portugal under Queen Maria I (died 20 March 1816) but not main. Also the Ottoman not a belligerent.

We should verify dates. Let's quickly check each via tool.

* The **Third Coalition** was formed in 1805 to oppose Napoleon’s French Empire. Its principal members were the United Kingdom, Austria, Russia, Sweden and the Kingdom of Naples (the Bourbon ruler of Naples was a close ally of Britain and Austria).  
* The coalition’s forces were defeated at the **Battle of Austerlitz** (2 December 1805), after which the coalition collapsed.  
* The heads of state listed above remained in power throughout the war and survived the conflict, dying in the years shown above.

**Gustav IV Adolf** or **Gustav IV Adolph**[1] (1 November 1778 – 7 February 1837) was King of Sweden from 1792 until he was deposed in a coup in 1809. He was also the last Swedish monarch to be the ruler of Finland.


The occupation of Finland in 1808–09 by Russian forces was the immediate cause of Gustav's violent overthrow by officers of his own army. Following his abdication on 29 March 1809, an Instrument of Government was hastily written, which severely circumscribed the powers of the monarchy. The "Instrument" was adopted in 1809 on 6 June, the National Day of Sweden now as well as in his time. It remained in force until replaced in 1974. The crown, now with strictly limited powers, passed to Gustav's uncle Charles XIII, who had no legitimate children; this want of heirs set into motion the quest for a successor, who was found the following year in the person of Jean-Baptiste Jules Bernadotte, the first monarch of the present royal family.[2]

functions.name: delegate
functions.desc:
Ask a capable helper for help looking up a piece of information or performing an action.
Do not simply repeat what the user said as instructions.
You should use this to break up complex user queries into multiple simpler steps.
NOTE: Helpers cannot see previous parts of your conversation.
